title: LUCID: Latent-Understanding Curriculum for Informed Domain Randomization in Humanoid Motion Tracking

scenes.title: A turning policy under real disturbances.
cues: This G one repeats a turning motion under manual pushes and zero-to-sixty-millisecond added delay.

scenes.title: Which feedback should set training difficulty?
scenes.eyebrow: 01 / DOMAIN RANDOMIZATION AS A FEEDBACK PROBLEM
cues: Randomization must balance exposure against learnability.
Joint error mixes execution mismatch with torque-generating offsets.
LUCID compares command and execution histories in a learned temporal space.

scenes.title: Compare histories. Guide the next training block.
cues: Issued commands pass through simulated delay and dynamics.
Command and execution histories enter the same frozen encoder.
Their normalized latent discrepancy guides the next training block.

scenes.title: Learn the comparison before policy training.
cues: First, a denoising temporal V A E learns to reconstruct clean motion from noisy windows.
We freeze its encoder, keeping the comparison fixed as the policy learns.

scenes.title: Adapt exposure across six training channels.
cues: Bounded P I adjusts intensity using the learned gap and accumulated error.
Two low-return blocks trigger a separate backoff.
One intensity sets all six training ranges for the next block.

scenes.title: Stress-test beyond the training delay range.
cues: Training uses up to forty milliseconds of added delay.
Frozen policies face sixty milliseconds on full held-out motions, fifty percent above the training maximum.

scenes.title: Unseen delay. Higher completion.
cues: Under unseen sixty-millisecond delay, completion rises from fifty-two point one percent with filtered-error P I to seventy-three point eight with LUCID.
That is a twenty-one point seven percentage-point gain.

scenes.title: The representation and feedback matter.
scenes.eyebrow: 07 / TEST THE REPRESENTATION AND LIVE FEEDBACK
cues: Denoising raises completion over ordinary reconstruction.
Live feedback also improves on one donor’s replayed schedule.

scenes.title: Inspect delay and push responses.
cues: These selected demonstrations combine forty milliseconds of added delay with scheduled pushes.
LUCID is on the left; filtered-error P I is on the right.
They show behavior under perturbation. Aggregate completion comes from separate benchmark trials.

scenes.title: Continuous deployment, separate benchmark.
scenes.eyebrow: 09 / PHYSICAL G1 · CONTINUOUS TAKE + PAPER EVIDENCE
cues: The same hardware recording has continued throughout this presentation.
Separately, the paper’s matched forty-millisecond test reports thirty-eight of sixty completions for LUCID, versus twenty-three for filtered-error P I.
Only the policy and low-level controller run onboard.

scenes.title: Train with feedback. Deploy the policy.
cues: Learn robustness during training. Deploy only the policy and low-level controller.

parallel_visualization.provenance: User-supplied visualization; descriptions below are transcribed from its visible overlays.
source_labels: Red remains after first native failure
parallel_visualization.interpretation: An evaluation replay illustrating parallel rollouts. No training update is shown. Green means no failure yet, not completed-trial success. Paper benchmark results are shown separately.

recorded_motion.source: Exact G1 model forward kinematics from captured qpos; matching synchronized source references. No new dynamics rollouts.

process_design.scope: Context evaluation replay and choreographed closing letter formation. Not comparison footage, measured formation-control performance or a recorded training update.
